correctness.rationale: Any palstar with exactly four 1s has either one positive palindromic block containing all four or two positive palindromic blocks with two each; zero-only blocks have even length. For gap word 0^a 1 0^b 1 0^c 1 0^d 1 0^e, two-block case iff b,d are even and c>=alpha+beta with c≡alpha+beta mod2, alpha=a mod2,beta=e mod2. One-block case iff b=d,c even,alpha=beta. Constructive paddings show both necessity and sufficiency. The case generating functions are G_II=(1+x)^2/(1-x)^5, G_I=(1+x)/(1-x)^4, intersection (1+x²)/((1-x²)(1-x)^3), so inclusion-exclusion yields (1+5x+x²+x³)/((1-x)^5(1+x)) and P_m=(4m^4-4m^3+2m²-8m+3-3(-1)^m)/24 for all integers m>=2. The leading coefficient gives density 1/4 within exactly-four-ones slice. Independently used a direct palindrome-cut dynamic program on EVERY fixed-weight-four binary word for lengths 4,6,...,22 and matched both gap criterion and counts 1,9,32,84,181,345,600,976,1505,2225. The exact parametric factorization, not the finite experiment, is the unrestricted proof.
